summary: American Olympic official Avery Brundage, an admirer of Hitler with antisemitic views, toured Nazi Germany and campaigned to defeat the US boycott of the 1936 Berlin Olympics, partly to win a seat on the IOC.

evidence.note: long Coubertin segment begins: birth 1863, Franco-Prussian war, reviving the Games
amateur rules framed as a way to keep working-class athletes out
Brundage born 1887 in Detroit to a stonecutter who left the family
construction superintendent in Chicago, later rebuilds a fortune after 1929 crash
AAU-NCAA deal lets colleges certify amateurs; later student-athlete case of 1955
after Hitler takes power in 1933, boycott push begins and Brundage opposes it
Brundage drops boycott support to please IOC leaders and gain a seat
1934 inspection trip to Germany with staged meetings with Jewish athletes
Sherrill sent to meet Hitler in 1935, proposes token Jewish athletes
Brundage's antisemitic correspondence and claims of a Jewish conspiracy
story closes at the August 1936 opening ceremony in Berlin

notes: Narrative ends at the 1936 opening ceremony; covered_span runs to 1975 only because of the lifetime rule, as his IOC presidency and death are barely mentioned. Ancient Olympics (about five minutes) treated as background. Transcript gives 1929 for his AOC presidency (usually given as 1928). Hate-speech warning for repeated reading of antisemitic letters by Brundage and Baillet-Latour.
